title: interactive-trace-scratchpad-alternatives
body:
Context:
Small exploration doc for alternative interaction patterns for the trace viewer. Goal is to capture several low-fidelity concepts we can prototype quickly and groom into backlog tickets. This is deliberately rough — thinking out loud for design + eng pairing on Tuesday.

Problem statement:
- Users (SREs, platform engineers, solutions eng) need to locate and triage high-latency requests across many concurrent traces quickly.
- Current waterfall + span list is dense; common tasks: find top-k slow spans, compare similar requests, annotate a span for post-mortem, and bookmark a request for later investigation.
- We want to reduce exploratory friction: fewer clicks, more keyboard, and in-context micro-summaries that avoid opening panels.

Design goals (priority order):
1) Surface likely root causes without forcing a trace-open cycle (fast triage).
2) Make span grouping and filtering composable and reversible (try patterns quickly).
3) Enable ephemeral notes / bookmarks (scratchpad) tied to trace session, not global storage.
4) Keep initial payload small — lazy hydrate heavy data.
5) Keyboard-first navigation and predictable focus handling for screen readers.

Concepts to prototype (brief):
A) Scratchpad Lanes (compact transient workspace)
- Feature: ephemeral horizontal lane above the waterfall where user drags spans (or presses "b" to bookmark). Each bookmark is a compact card: span name, latency, service tag, 3-line micro-summary auto-extracted.
- Interaction: drag-and-drop from waterfall, keyboard: select span (j/k), press b -> adds card to scratchpad. Esc clears selection.
- Use: short-lived investigations, shareable copy-paste snapshot (copy button exports md).
- Implementation note: cards store only span id and a short cached summary; full hydration only on demand.

B) Lane Sampling & Collapse (visual simplification for dense traces)
- Feature: heuristic sampling of repetitive spans into one collapsible lane tile (shows count, p50/p95).
- Interaction: hover opens mini-timeline for that span group; click expands to show up to N real spans inline.
- Heuristic: group by (service, span name, resource hash) within trace window.
- Perf: server-side summary endpoint for grouped spans to avoid sending full list for mega-traces.

C) Inline Micro-Summaries (hover / peek)
- Feature: hover over a span yields 3-line auto summary (why slow? e.g., downstream call X at 90ms, db query Y p95 120ms).
- Sources: combine span annotations + sampled logs + cached KV metrics.
- Accessibility: make peek accessible via keyboard (enter/space to open peek) and ensure ARIA live region announces key details.

D) Trace Deltas (compare two traces side-by-side but in same lane)
- Feature: small diff overlay that highlights where two traces deviate: extra spans, longer spans, missing caches.
- Interaction: select base trace, then ctrl-click another trace from search results to open inline comparison ribbon. Ribbons are thin lanes with color-coded diff marks.

E) Keyboard-first Probe Mode
- Feature: quick probe mode toggled with "p" where user can run small test probes (replay headers, run synthetic) and attach results as ephemeral spans.
- Use case: reproduce a bad header combo or client path quickly.

Wireframe notes (sketch directions for design):
- Top header row: left: search + timeline scrubber; center: scratchpad lanes (collapsed by default, expand on hover); right: quick actions (bookmark, annotate, compare).
- Waterfall: condensed tick marks, rounded span bars, right-aligned token for p50/p95 in small font.
- Hover card: left column small timeline sparkline, middle textual summary, right column quick actions (copy span id, add to scratchpad, open log).
- Colors: keep warm palette for latency hotspots (amber > orange > deep red) but add a neutral blue for grouped tiles to avoid salience confusion.

Edge cases and UX gotchas:
- Massive traces (1000+ spans): default to lane sampling with an on-screen heuristic banner: "Trace condensed — expand groups to view detail". Provide a toggle to force full hydration.
- Long span names: truncate with ellipsis; tooltip shows full string and searchable tokenization.
- Span re-ordering when grouped: keep original timeline position visible via thin ghost markers when collapsed groups are opened.
- Collisions: dragging to scratchpad should not scroll waterfall unexpectedly; use keyboard alternative for precise add.

Performance model and implementation notes for eng:
- Lazy hydration: initial trace payload includes summary objects for spans (span id, name, start, duration, parent id, tags) and small group summaries. Full logs/annotations fetched via separate endpoint on open.
- Server endpoints needed: /trace/:id/summary, /trace/:id/grouped-spans?window=..., /span/:id/logs?sample=1.
- Cost consideration: group summaries are cheap; full-span logs are expensive (rate-limit per session).

Accessibility checklist (minimal):
- Keyboard nav: j/k for next/prev span, enter to open peek, b to add to scratchpad, shift+? to show hotkeys.
- ARIA: hover peeks as dialogs with role="dialog" and aria-modal=false; live region for dynamic latency alerts.
- Color contrast: test hotspot palette at 4.5:1 for labels.

Grooming backlog (initial tickets and rough sizing):
- TRACE-427: scratchpad lanes basic (ui + add/remove) — 3 devs, 5 sprint-days — acceptance: add/remove via keyboard and drag, export md.
- TRACE-428: grouped-lane sampling backend + UI condensed tile — 2 devs, 6 sprint-days — acceptance: heuristic groups for 500-span traces, group expand shows up to 50 items.
- TRACE-429: hover micro-summary (frontend + summary API) — 1 dev, 3 sprint-days — acceptance: hover returns summary within 150ms for common traces.
- TRACE-430: keyboard probe mode (skeleton) — 1 dev, 4 sprint-days — acceptance: toggle probe mode and attach synthetic span to current trace sandbox.
- UX-311: accessibility pass for trace viewer (audit + fixes) — 0.5 dev, 2 design-days.

Acceptance criteria examples (scratchpad):
1) Bookmark via keyboard: selecting a span and pressing 'b' adds an item to scratchpad and shows a transient toast with copy link action.
2) Export: clicking export on scratchpad produces a markdown blob with span id, short summary, and permalinks.
3) Persistence: scratchpad state persists only for the browser session (localStorage); edge case: user navigates away -> show banner "scratchpad saved for 24h?" (opt-in).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should scratchpad cards support free-form notes or only auto-summaries? (Tradeoff: UX speed vs backend storage + sync).
- Grouping heuristic threshold: what cardinality triggers sampling? Default 200 spans? Ops input needed.
- Should micro-summaries be ML generated (cost) or rule-based extraction (cheap)? Try rule-based first, add ML if coverage poor.

Next steps (short):
- Pair Aisha + Miguel to mock quick Figma frames for A, B, C concepts (Tue 10am).
- Dev sync: Ben to sketch API shapes and cost envelope for grouped summary endpoint (Thu).
- Create minimal prototype ticket TRACE-427 with stub UI and localStorage-based scratchpad for usability testing.

Notes-to-self / random crumbs:
- Consider micro-copy: "Add to scratchpad" vs "Clip span". "Clip" is playful but might confuse.
- Could reuse the existing timeline scrubber component from console/timeline repo (ask infra owners).

References:
- Existing trace viewer tickets (search: TRACE-*)
- Quick prototype: https://codesandbox.io/s/compact-waterfall-prototype (design demo)

End.
